\section[lorsque]{lorsque — when (careful style)}

\label{lesson:FR-C269-lorsque}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the French for lastly, then the French for to finish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: lorsque}
\textbf{lorsque} — \textquotedblleft{}when (careful style)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Lorsque je suis arrivé, la fête avait déjà commencé.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{When I arrived, the party had already started.}
\end{quote}

It means \emph{quand} in a time clause, a little more written. Before a vowel it becomes \emph{lorsqu'}: \emph{lorsqu'il pleut}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lorsque} joins \emph{lors} \textquotedblleft{}then\textquotedblright{} and \emph{que} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Lors} is traced to Latin \emph{illā hōrā} \textquotedblleft{}at that hour\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{hōra} \textquotedblleft{}hour\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[dès que]{dès que — as soon as}

\label{lesson:FR-C269-des-que}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the French for to finish, then the French for when.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dès que}
\textbf{dès que} — \textquotedblleft{}as soon as\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dès que le film a fini, nous sommes partis.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{As soon as the film ended, we left.}
\end{quote}

For an event still to come, the future follows: \emph{dès qu'il arrivera, on mangera}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dès} is usually traced to Late Latin \emph{dē ex} \textquotedblleft{}from out of\textquotedblright{}, the prepositions \emph{dē} \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ex} \textquotedblleft{}out of\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short) run together; EtymDB lists no parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[au moment où]{au moment où — at the moment when, right as}

\label{lesson:FR-C269-au-moment-ou}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the French for when, then the French for as soon as.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: au moment où}
\textbf{au moment où} — \textquotedblleft{}at the moment when, right as\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Au moment où je sortais, le téléphone a sonné.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Right as I was going out, the phone rang.}
\end{quote}

After \emph{moment}, French says \emph{où}, not \emph{quand}: \emph{au moment où il est entré}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{moment} comes from Latin \emph{mōmentum} (EtymDB), taken over as a learned word; Lewis \& Short gloss it \textquotedblleft{}movement, motion\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{movēre} \textquotedblleft{}to move\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\section[aussitôt]{aussitôt — at once, immediately}

\label{lesson:FR-C269-aussitot}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the French for as soon as, then the French for at the moment when.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: aussitôt}
\textbf{aussitôt} — \textquotedblleft{}at once, immediately\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il a vu la lettre et il l'a aussitôt ouverte.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He saw the letter and opened it at once.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Aussitôt que} means the same as \emph{dès que}: as soon as.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aussitôt} joins \emph{aussi} \textquotedblleft{}so\textquotedblright{} and \emph{tôt} \textquotedblleft{}early\textquotedblright{}; \emph{tôt} is usually traced to Latin \emph{tostum} \textquotedblleft{}scorched, burnt\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{torrēre} \textquotedblleft{}to roast\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[tandis que]{tandis que — while, whereas}

\label{lesson:FR-C269-tandis-que}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the French for at the moment when, then the French for at once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: tandis que}
\textbf{tandis que} — \textquotedblleft{}while, whereas\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il lisait tandis que sa sœur jouait du piano.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He was reading while his sister was playing the piano.}
\end{quote}

Two uses: time, 'while', and contrast, 'whereas': \emph{il aime la mer, tandis que je préfère la montagne}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tandis} is inherited from Latin \emph{tam diū} \textquotedblleft{}for so long\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{tam} \textquotedblleft{}so\textquotedblright{} and \emph{diū} \textquotedblleft{}for a long time\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
